summary: Verified the drawer->page refactor for Super Admin org management. Logged in as super_admin (via cookie injection to skip MFA), landed on /super-admin, confirmed 10 org cards present with data-testid=manage-org-{id} buttons, and NO drawer markup remains in the DOM. Clicking Manage navigates to /super-admin/orgs/{orgId} (verified with IDOR Test Org B). New page renders correctly with: header (name/status badge/jurisdiction/signup date), Back to Organisations link (data-testid=back-to-orgs-btn), Suspend button (toggle-status-btn), stat cards (Users=2, Meetings=4), full Billing & Usage form (all 8 fields wired to their existing data-testids: billing-tier-select, billing-included-hours-input, billing-is-trial-checkbox, billing-trial-ends-input, billing-stripe-customer-input, billing-stripe-status-select, billing-next-payment-input, billing-notes-textarea, save-billing-btn), usage history section, and Users section with Add User + Invite Admin + per-user edit/delete testids. Back button returns to /super-admin. Direct navigation to /super-admin/orgs/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 renders graceful 'Organisation not found' with working back link (data-testid=back-to-orgs-btn-notfound). Save Billing was clicked (200 OK, form re-hydrated). Add User modal opens and shows form. No JS runtime errors; only 2 benign 404 console warnings (likely optional asset).
critical_code_review_comments: SuperAdminOrgDetail.js is 939 lines — over the 700-line soft limit. Consider extracting the three modals (Create User, Invite Admin, Delete Confirm) and the Billing form into their own files. Same shared components (TierBadge, StripeStatusBadge, UsageBar, StatusBadge, RoleBadge, PRICING_TIERS, STRIPE_STATUS_*) are now duplicated verbatim between SuperAdminDashboard.js and SuperAdminOrgDetail.js — extract into /components/superadmin/ to eliminate DRY violation.

loadOrg + loadUsers + loadUsageHistory fire three parallel requests on mount — fine, but if the org 404s, loadUsers and loadUsageHistory still fire and silently 404 too (they swallow errors into empty arrays). Consider gating them on loadOrg success to avoid the extra noise in browser console (this matches the 2 x 404 observed in test).
